Upstream GCC commit 5d419c69ce2e6b86d7da75f18736904885674219 (PR libstdc++/124370) stops std::bitset wide-character stream extraction from sizing its buffer without sizeof(wchar_t). The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, re-expressed against the 14.2.0 operator>>. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-115455

Upstream GCC commit 2fd8866591b5aea7098835f80ab7e176382175ae makes std::vector<bool> constructors check the element count against max_size() before sizing the bit array, so the word count cannot wrap. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, without the from_range constructor hunk, which GCC 14.2.0 does not have. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114691

Upstream GCC commit c1f32b67510f6f9998deadaef5090b6663adb979 sizes the parallel std::search border table one element larger so the border computation cannot index past it. CVE-2026-102554 is fixed in Guava 33.7.2. The Guava copies reported here are embedded inside other jars and cannot be upgraded on their own: 14.0.1 inside ambari-metrics-common 2.7.0.0.0 (ambari-metrics-emitter extension), 30.1.1-jre shaded inside hadoop-client-runtime 3.3.6, and 33.2.1-jre (Druid 36) or 33.4.8-jre (Druid 37) inside iceberg-bundled-guava (druid-iceberg-extensions). The latest Iceberg release (iceberg-bundled-guava 1.12.0) still bundles Guava 33.7.1-jre, and the latest hadoop-client-runtime (3.5.0) bundles 33.4.8-jre. The issue requires Java deserialization of an attacker-crafted CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet or MapMakerInternalMap stream; reachability through these extensions has not been assessed. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94

CVE-2026-102554 is fixed in Guava 33.7.2. The Guava copies reported here are embedded inside other jars and cannot be upgraded on their own: 14.0.1 inside ambari-metrics-common 2.7.0.0.0 (ambari-metrics-emitter extension), 30.1.1-jre shaded inside hadoop-client-runtime 3.3.6, 32.0.1-jre inside hadoop-shaded-guava 1.4.0 (druid-ranger-security), 32.1.3-jre shaded into the opentelemetry-emitter jar from that module's shade.guava.version, and 33.2.1-jre (Druid 36) or 33.4.8-jre (Druid 37) inside iceberg-bundled-guava (druid-iceberg-extensions). The latest Iceberg release (iceberg-bundled-guava 1.12.0) still bundles Guava 33.7.1-jre, and the latest hadoop-client-runtime (3.5.0) bundles 33.4.8-jre. hadoop-shaded-guava 1.6.0 bundles Guava 33.7.2-jre, and the opentelemetry-emitter property can be moved to 33.7.2-jre; images built before those pins still ship the versions listed here. Druid 38's managed guava.version pin is 33.5.0-jre, which is not one of those embedded copies; moving that pin to 33.7.2 requires a new druid-38 package revision. The issue requires Java deserialization of an attacker-crafted CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet or MapMakerInternalMap stream; reachability through these extensions has not been assessed. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94

Debian security tracker: fixed in unstable by the same change as CVE-2026-85091, which is upstream zlib commit df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148. That change resets the stream input pointer and available input after a failed write() in gz_write(), so a later gz* write cannot use the stale caller buffer. This package build includes an adaptation of that upstream change for the zlib 1.3.1 code base. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-76844

JLine 3.9.0 classes are shaded inside hadoop-client-runtime pulled by Druid's Hadoop-based extensions. Druid does not start an interactive JLine shell or load org.jline reader builtins in the broker/historical/middleManager runtime; the shaded copies are not on an attacker-reachable execute path. Dependency management pins org.jline modules to 3.30.15 for non-shaded copies.

CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

CVE-2026-56741 is the CVE identifier for the JLine3 Telnet server (remote-telnet module) CPU-exhaustion DoS tracked as GHSA-2r2c-cx56-8933: TelnetIO.handleNAWS() accepts attacker-supplied NAWS terminal dimensions with only a lower bound and drives redisplay() up to 65534 iterations per event. Druid does not instantiate or expose a JLine Telnet server; jline is bundled as a transitive dependency (via the org.jline:jline uber-jar) for CLI line-reading only. The telnet server code is present in the uber-jar but is never loaded or executed in Druid's runtime. The fix exists only in jline 4.x (all 3.x versions are affected) and upgrading is a major version change incompatible with the current dependency tree.

Integer underflow and heap out-of-bounds read in berval2tl_data() in the LDAP KDB backend plugin (plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c). Triggering requires a KDC or kadmind configured with an LDAP database backend whose backend returns a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2; that data originates from the trusted KDB datastore, not from an external Kerberos protocol client, so it cannot be controlled by an adversary. Debian marks this unimportant (bug 1139821) with no security impact and notes it does not cross any security boundary.
